audit_status.source_base: Greek Ephesians text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for worthy walk, one body/Spirit/Lord/trust/baptism/Divine, gifts, body maturity, old/new human, truth in love.

verses.restored: Therefore I, the prisoner in the Lord, appeal to you to walk worthily of the calling with which you were called,

familiar.text: I therefore, the prisoner of the Lord, beseech you that ye walk worthy of the vocation wherewith ye are called,

modern.text: As a prisoner in the Lord, then, I urge you to walk in a manner worthy of the calling you have received:

original.text: Παρακαλῶ οὖν ὑμᾶς ἐγὼ ὁ δέσμιος ἐν κυρίῳ ἀξίως περιπατῆσαι τῆς κλήσεως ἧς ἐκλήθητε,

verses.restored: with all humility and gentleness, with patience, bearing with one another in love,

familiar.text: With all lowliness and meekness, with longsuffering, forbearing one another in love;

modern.text: with all humility and gentleness, with patience, bearing with one another in love,

original.text: μετὰ πάσης ταπεινοφροσύνης καὶ πραΰτητος, μετὰ μακροθυμίας, ἀνεχόμενοι ἀλλήλων ἐν ἀγάπῃ,

verses.restored: being eager to keep the oneness of the Spirit in the bond of peace.

familiar.text: Endeavouring to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.

modern.text: and with diligence to preserve the unity of the Spirit through the bond of peace.

original.text: σπουδάζοντες τηρεῖν τὴν ἑνότητα τοῦ πνεύματος ἐν τῷ συνδέσμῳ τῆς εἰρήνης·

verses.restored: One body and one Spirit, just as also you were called in one hope of your calling;

familiar.text: There is one body, and one Spirit, even as ye are called in one hope of your calling;

modern.text: There is one body and one Spirit, just as you were called to one hope when you were called;

original.text: ἓν σῶμα καὶ ἓν πνεῦμα, καθὼς καὶ ἐκλήθητε ἐν μιᾷ ἐλπίδι τῆς κλήσεως ὑμῶν·

verses.restored: one Lord, one trust, one baptism;

familiar.text: One Lord, one faith, one baptism,

modern.text: one Lord, one faith, one baptism;

original.text: εἷς κύριος, μία πίστις, ἓν βάπτισμα·

verses.restored: one Divine and Father of all, the One over all and through all and in all.

familiar.text: One God and Father of all, who is above all, and through all, and in you all.

modern.text: one God and Father of all, who is over all and through all and in all.

original.text: εἷς θεὸς καὶ πατὴρ πάντων, ὁ ἐπὶ πάντων καὶ διὰ πάντων καὶ ἐν ⸀πᾶσιν.

verses.restored: But to each one of us grace was given according to the measure of the gift of Messiah.

familiar.text: But unto every one of us is given grace according to the measure of the gift of Christ.

modern.text: Now to each one of us grace has been given according to the measure of the gift of Christ.

original.text: Ἑνὶ δὲ ἑκάστῳ ἡμῶν ἐδόθη ⸀ἡ χάρις κατὰ τὸ μέτρον τῆς δωρεᾶς τοῦ Χριστοῦ.

verses.restored: Therefore it says: Having ascended on high, he led captivity captive; he gave gifts to humans.

familiar.text: Wherefore he saith, When he ascended up on high, he led captivity captive, and gave gifts unto men.

modern.text: This is why it says: “When He ascended on high, He led captives away, and gave gifts to men.”

original.text: διὸ λέγει· Ἀναβὰς εἰς ὕψος ᾐχμαλώτευσεν αἰχμαλωσίαν, ⸀ἔδωκεν δόματα τοῖς ἀνθρώποις.

verses.restored: Now this, he ascended, what is it except that he also descended into the lower parts of the earth?

familiar.text: (Now that he ascended, what is it but that he also descended first into the lower parts of the earth?

modern.text: What does “He ascended” mean, except that He also descended to the lower parts of the earth?

original.text: τὸ δὲ Ἀνέβη τί ἐστιν εἰ μὴ ὅτι καὶ ⸀κατέβη εἰς τὰ κατώτερα μέρη τῆς γῆς;

verses.restored: The One who descended is also the One who ascended far above all the heavens, so that he might fill all things.

familiar.text: He that descended is the same also that ascended up far above all heavens, that he might fill all things.)

modern.text: He who descended is the very One who ascended above all the heavens, in order to fill all things.

original.text: ὁ καταβὰς αὐτός ἐστιν καὶ ὁ ἀναβὰς ὑπεράνω πάντων τῶν οὐρανῶν, ἵνα πληρώσῃ τὰ πάντα.

verses.restored: And he gave some as apostles, some prophets, some announcers of good news, some shepherds and teachers,

familiar.text: And he gave some, apostles; and some, prophets; and some, evangelists; and some, pastors and teachers;

modern.text: And it was He who gave some to be apostles, some to be prophets, some to be evangelists, and some to be pastors and teachers,

original.text: καὶ αὐτὸς ἔδωκεν τοὺς μὲν ἀποστόλους, τοὺς δὲ προφήτας, τοὺς δὲ εὐαγγελιστάς, τοὺς δὲ ποιμένας καὶ διδασκάλους,

verses.restored: toward the equipping/restoration of the holy ones, into work of service, into building up the body of Messiah,

familiar.text: For the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry, for the edifying of the body of Christ:

modern.text: to equip the saints for works of ministry and to build up the body of Christ,

original.text: πρὸς τὸν καταρτισμὸν τῶν ἁγίων εἰς ἔργον διακονίας, εἰς οἰκοδομὴν τοῦ σώματος τοῦ Χριστοῦ,

verses.restored: until we all arrive into the oneness of the trust and of the knowledge of the Son of the Divine, into mature/complete humanity, into measure of stature of the fullness of Messiah,

familiar.text: Till we all come in the unity of the faith, and of the knowledge of the Son of God, unto a perfect man, unto the measure of the stature of the fulness of Christ:

modern.text: until we all reach unity in the faith and in the knowledge of the Son of God, as we mature to the full measure of the stature of Christ.

original.text: μέχρι καταντήσωμεν οἱ πάντες εἰς τὴν ἑνότητα τῆς πίστεως καὶ τῆς ἐπιγνώσεως τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ, εἰς ἄνδρα τέλειον, εἰς μέτρον ἡλικίας τοῦ πληρώματος τοῦ Χριστοῦ,

verses.restored: so that we may no longer be infants, tossed by waves and carried around by every wind of teaching, by human trickery, by craftiness toward the schemes of error,

familiar.text: That we henceforth be no more children, tossed to and fro, and carried about with every wind of doctrine, by the sleight of men, and cunning craftiness, whereby they lie in wait to deceive;

modern.text: Then we will no longer be infants, tossed about by the waves and carried around by every wind of teaching and by the clever cunning of men in their deceitful scheming.

original.text: ἵνα μηκέτι ὦμεν νήπιοι, κλυδωνιζόμενοι καὶ περιφερόμενοι παντὶ ἀνέμῳ τῆς διδασκαλίας ἐν τῇ κυβείᾳ τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐν πανουργίᾳ πρὸς τὴν μεθοδείαν τῆς πλάνης,

verses.restored: but truthing in love, we may grow up in all things into him who is the head, Messiah,

familiar.text: But speaking the truth in love, may grow up into him in all things, which is the head, even Christ:

modern.text: Instead, speaking the truth in love, we will in all things grow up into Christ Himself, who is the head.

original.text: ἀληθεύοντες δὲ ἐν ἀγάπῃ αὐξήσωμεν εἰς αὐτὸν τὰ πάντα, ὅς ἐστιν ἡ κεφαλή, ⸀Χριστός,

verses.restored: from whom the whole body, joined and held together through every supporting ligament, according to working in measure of each single part, makes the growth of the body into building itself up in love.

familiar.text: From whom the whole body fitly joined together and compacted by that which every joint supplieth, according to the effectual working in the measure of every part, maketh increase of the body unto the edifying of itself in love.

modern.text: From Him the whole body, fitted and held together by every supporting ligament, grows and builds itself up in love through the work of each individual part. New Life in Christ (Colossians 3:1–17)

original.text: ἐξ οὗ πᾶν τὸ σῶμα συναρμολογούμενον καὶ συμβιβαζόμενον διὰ πάσης ἁφῆς τῆς ἐπιχορηγίας κατʼ ἐνέργειαν ἐν μέτρῳ ἑνὸς ἑκάστου μέρους τὴν αὔξησιν τοῦ σώματος ποιεῖται εἰς οἰκοδομὴν ἑαυτοῦ ἐν ἀγάπῃ.

verses.restored: Therefore this I say and testify in the Lord: no longer walk as the nations also walk, in futility of their mind,

familiar.text: This I say therefore, and testify in the Lord, that ye henceforth walk not as other Gentiles walk, in the vanity of their mind,

modern.text: So I tell you this, and insist on it in the Lord, that you must no longer walk as the Gentiles do, in the futility of their thinking.

original.text: Τοῦτο οὖν λέγω καὶ μαρτύρομαι ἐν κυρίῳ, μηκέτι ὑμᾶς περιπατεῖν καθὼς καὶ ⸀τὰ ἔθνη περιπατεῖ ἐν ματαιότητι τοῦ νοὸς αὐτῶν,

verses.restored: having been darkened in understanding, alienated from the life of the Divine because of the ignorance being in them, because of the hardness of their heart,

familiar.text: Having the understanding darkened, being alienated from the life of God through the ignorance that is in them, because of the blindness of their heart:

modern.text: They are darkened in their understanding and alienated from the life of God because of the ignorance that is in them due to the hardness of their hearts.

original.text: ⸀ἐσκοτωμένοι τῇ διανοίᾳ ὄντες, ἀπηλλοτριωμένοι τῆς ζωῆς τοῦ θεοῦ, διὰ τὴν ἄγνοιαν τὴν οὖσαν ἐν αὐτοῖς, διὰ τὴν πώρωσιν τῆς καρδίας αὐτῶν,

verses.restored: who, having become callous, handed themselves over to shameless excess, into practice of every uncleanness in greed.

familiar.text: Who being past feeling have given themselves over unto lasciviousness, to work all uncleanness with greediness.

modern.text: Having lost all sense of shame, they have given themselves over to sensuality for the practice of every kind of impurity, with a craving for more.

original.text: οἵτινες ἀπηλγηκότες ἑαυτοὺς παρέδωκαν τῇ ἀσελγείᾳ εἰς ἐργασίαν ἀκαθαρσίας πάσης ἐν πλεονεξίᾳ.

verses.restored: But you did not learn Messiah this way,

familiar.text: But ye have not so learned Christ;

modern.text: But this is not the way you came to know Christ.

original.text: ὑμεῖς δὲ οὐχ οὕτως ἐμάθετε τὸν Χριστόν,

verses.restored: if indeed you heard him and were taught in him, just as truth is in Jesus,

familiar.text: If so be that ye have heard him, and have been taught by him, as the truth is in Jesus:

modern.text: Surely you heard of Him and were taught in Him—in keeping with the truth that is in Jesus—

original.text: εἴ γε αὐτὸν ἠκούσατε καὶ ἐν αὐτῷ ἐδιδάχθητε, καθώς ἐστιν ἀλήθεια ἐν τῷ Ἰησοῦ,

verses.restored: to put away, according to the former conduct, the old human, being corrupted according to desires of deceit,

familiar.text: That ye put off concerning the former conversation the old man, which is corrupt according to the deceitful lusts;

modern.text: to put off your former way of life, your old self, which is being corrupted by its deceitful desires;

original.text: ἀποθέσθαι ὑμᾶς κατὰ τὴν προτέραν ἀναστροφὴν τὸν παλαιὸν ἄνθρωπον τὸν φθειρόμενον κατὰ τὰς ἐπιθυμίας τῆς ἀπάτης,

verses.restored: and to be renewed in the spirit of your mind,

familiar.text: And be renewed in the spirit of your mind;

modern.text: to be renewed in the spirit of your minds;

original.text: ἀνανεοῦσθαι δὲ τῷ πνεύματι τοῦ νοὸς ὑμῶν,

verses.restored: and to put on the new human, created according to the Divine in righteousness/justice and holiness of truth.

familiar.text: And that ye put on the new man, which after God is created in righteousness and true holiness.

modern.text: and to put on the new self, created to be like God in true righteousness and holiness.

original.text: καὶ ἐνδύσασθαι τὸν καινὸν ἄνθρωπον τὸν κατὰ θεὸν κτισθέντα ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ καὶ ὁσιότητι τῆς ἀληθείας.

verses.restored: Therefore, having put away falsehood, speak truth each one with one's neighbor, because we are members of one another.

familiar.text: Wherefore putting away lying, speak every man truth with his neighbour: for we are members one of another.

modern.text: Therefore each of you must put off falsehood and speak truthfully to his neighbor, for we are all members of one another.

original.text: Διὸ ἀποθέμενοι τὸ ψεῦδος λαλεῖτε ἀλήθειαν ἕκαστος μετὰ τοῦ πλησίον αὐτοῦ, ὅτι ἐσμὲν ἀλλήλων μέλη.

verses.restored: Be angry and do not sin/misalign; do not let the sun set upon your provocation,

familiar.text: Be ye angry, and sin not: let not the sun go down upon your wrath:

modern.text: “Be angry, yet do not sin.” Do not let the sun set upon your anger,

original.text: ὀργίζεσθε καὶ μὴ ἁμαρτάνετε· ὁ ἥλιος μὴ ἐπιδυέτω ⸀ἐπὶ παροργισμῷ ὑμῶν,

verses.restored: nor give place/opportunity to the adversarial one.

familiar.text: Neither give place to the devil.

modern.text: and do not give the devil a foothold.

original.text: μηδὲ δίδοτε τόπον τῷ διαβόλῳ.

verses.restored: Let the one stealing steal no longer, but rather labor, working with one's own hands the good, so that one may have to share with the one having need.

familiar.text: Let him that stole steal no more: but rather let him labour, working with his hands the thing which is good, that he may have to give to him that needeth.

modern.text: He who has been stealing must steal no longer, but must work, doing good with his own hands, that he may have something to share with the one in need.

original.text: ὁ κλέπτων μηκέτι κλεπτέτω, μᾶλλον δὲ κοπιάτω ἐργαζόμενος ⸂ταῖς ἰδίαις χερσὶν τὸ ἀγαθόν⸃, ἵνα ἔχῃ μεταδιδόναι τῷ χρείαν ἔχοντι.

verses.restored: Let no rotten word go out from your mouth, but only what is good for building up as need requires, so that it may give grace to those hearing.

familiar.text: Let no corrupt communication proceed out of your mouth, but that which is good to the use of edifying, that it may minister grace unto the hearers.

modern.text: Let no unwholesome talk come out of your mouths, but only what is helpful for building up the one in need and bringing grace to those who listen.

original.text: πᾶς λόγος σαπρὸς ἐκ τοῦ στόματος ὑμῶν μὴ ἐκπορευέσθω, ἀλλὰ εἴ τις ἀγαθὸς πρὸς οἰκοδομὴν τῆς χρείας, ἵνα δῷ χάριν τοῖς ἀκούουσιν.

verses.restored: And do not grieve the holy Spirit of the Divine, in whom you were sealed into the day of redemption/release.

familiar.text: And grieve not the holy Spirit of God, whereby ye are sealed unto the day of redemption.

modern.text: And do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God, in whom you were sealed for the day of redemption.

original.text: καὶ μὴ λυπεῖτε τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον τοῦ θεοῦ, ἐν ᾧ ἐσφραγίσθητε εἰς ἡμέραν ἀπολυτρώσεως.

verses.restored: Let all bitterness and fury and anger and shouting and slander be taken away from you, with all harmfulness.

familiar.text: Let all bitterness, and wrath, and anger, and clamour, and evil speaking, be put away from you, with all malice:

modern.text: Get rid of all bitterness, rage and anger, outcry and slander, along with every form of malice.

original.text: πᾶσα πικρία καὶ θυμὸς καὶ ὀργὴ καὶ κραυγὴ καὶ βλασφημία ἀρθήτω ἀφʼ ὑμῶν σὺν πάσῃ κακίᾳ.

verses.restored: Become kind to one another, tenderhearted, graciously forgiving each other, just as also the Divine in Messiah graciously forgave you.

familiar.text: And be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ’s sake hath forgiven you.

modern.text: Be kind and tenderhearted to one another, forgiving each other just as in Christ God forgave you.

original.text: ⸀γίνεσθε εἰς ἀλλήλους χρηστοί, εὔσπλαγχνοι, χαριζόμενοι ἑαυτοῖς καθὼς καὶ ὁ θεὸς ἐν Χριστῷ ἐχαρίσατο ⸀ὑμῖν.

translation_notes: Truthing in love preserves the verbal force of aletheuontes in 4:15: truth is practiced relationally, not merely possessed as correctness.
New human language is communal and ethical, not a rejection of embodied life.
